body: Interesting one, I'll take a look!
I am pretty sure there is an easy fix for this one, but I need to check
I tried one easy fix I was able to come up with, but that made things even worse :-D

Indeed I had a wrong understanding of the problem. 
Looking more now

The problem is solvable, but we need our JUnit 5 extension to be smarter about how is sets up Quarkus bootstraping.
Essentially if we add something like:

```
runnerBuilder.addAdditionalApplicationArchive(new AdditionalDependency(locationOfAbstractClass, false, true, true));
```

to `QuarkusTestExtension#doJavaStart` then the problem goes away.

@stuartwdouglas @aloubyansky does this make sense? If so, do we have any good way of doing this (instead of doing some classpath scanning and manual figuring out the location)?
I tried something like that, but got other classloading errors (something with H2 driver, no longer remember exactly). But my attempt was very naive.
A super naive test like what I described worked for me.
In that case, I should probably extend the reproducer to include some of the database stuff. Tomorrow, hopefully :-)
@geoand `locationOfAbstractClass` is each super class in the hierarchy?
